summary: Preinstall dropper fetches opaque content from Pastebin and an anonymous paste host
details: The package is advertised as a one-line numeric clamp utility but ships a preinstall lifecycle hook (`node setup.js`) that, on `npm install`, fetches bytes from https://pastebin.com/raw/z6K1Rg8J and https://calcal.ru/p/t5edjvR/raw (first-successful wins), writes them to a random path under the OS tmpdir, and passes the resulting file to a `run()` function. The destinations are author-mutable paste hosts unrelated to the package's stated publisher, and the content is unpinned and unverified. In version 1.0.2 the `run()` function is an empty stub so the fetched bytes are not executed, but the full dropper scaffolding — preinstall trigger, dual-source fetch with failover, staging under tmpdir, handoff to a runner — is present and reachable. Error reporting is obfuscated: HTTP failures surface as `Error #<status*13579>` and `process.exit(1)`, concealing which remote host failed and masking that preinstall is reaching Pastebin/calcal.ru. None of this behavior is justified by a 7-line clamp utility.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
